name: Veronika Vrecionová - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2020/2220 as regards specific measures under the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) to provide additional assistance to Member States affected by natural disasters
part_text:
The European Parliament backs a plan to let countries hit by natural disasters since 1 January 2024 use money from the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development more flexibly. The money would help farmers, forest owners and small rural businesses recover, including one-off payments of up to 42,000 euros per person. Parliament accepts the Commission's proposal without changes. It is a response to floods, droughts and wildfires that have destroyed farm and forestry production and cut incomes in rural areas.

- What changes: rural development money can be redirected to disaster aid, with one-off payments up to 42,000 euros.
- Who it affects: farmers, forest owners and small rural businesses in countries hit by disasters since 1 January 2024.
- What happens next: Parliament approved the plan; the Council must now formally adopt it before it becomes law.
